To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the frequency of Ca 2+ oscillations evoked by angiotensin in adrenal glomerulose cells is modulated by Ca2+ influx mechanisms, but that these mechanisms are differentially activated by low versus high angiotensin concentrations.
Ca2+ oscillatory frequency is modulated by VSCC activation, whereas the nonoscillating Ca2+ response is regulated mainly by capacitative Ca2+, entry.

Ca2+ oscillatory frequency is regulated by the balance between Ca2+ influx and efflux through VSCCs and the capacitative Ca 2+ entry pathway, and that the latter mechanism is dominant at higher concentrations of the agonist, Ang II.
In summary, our research is concerned with
Ca2+ signaling mechanisms in adrenal glomerulose cells.
the regulation of the Ca2+ signaling pathway in adrenal glomerulose cells.
Ca2+ oscillatory behavior and its modulation by Ca2+ influx mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the frequency of Ca oscillations is determined by the rate at which Ca2+ enters the cell, which is determined by the concentration of agonist, which in turn, determines how much Ca2+ is released by IP3.

the VSCC-mediated influx of calcium is the main determinant of the oscillatory behavior of the intracellular calcium concentration, whereas the capacitative Ca entry pathway is the main determinant for the plateau response.
the frequency of Ca(2+) oscillations induced by Ang II in glomerulosa cell is modulated by VSCCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the frequency of Ang II-stimulated intracellular Ca2+-oscillation is modulated by Ca2+ influx mechanisms in adrenal glomerulose cells.
the frequency of Ang II-stimulated [Ca2+]c oscillations is modulated by Ca2+ influx via VSCCs, whereas the amplitude is determined by inositol trphosphate-mediated Ca2+ release.
the Ca2+ influx mechanism is a key determinant of Ca2+ spikin frequency, and the Ca2+ release mechanism is a key factor for the amplitude of Ca2+ spikes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of Ca2+ signaling by Ang II is a complex phenomenon, involving multiple pathways and a number of feedback mechanisms.
Ca2+ oscillatory responses to low Ang II concentrations are mediated by a mechanism that is sensitive to dihydropyidines and is dependent on Ca2+ influx.
VSCCs play a major role in regulating Ca2+ oscillatory responses, but they are not the only pathway that mediates Ca2+ influx in adrenal glomerulose cells.
